Lost Castle Sentry
I was guarding the castle gate, and when I opened my eyes I was in this forest. Where has my castle gone?
There are iron drums rolling about in the rocky fields. They reek of oil, and they're not from our castle stores.
At night I saw blue lights floating and turning above the woods. You can't fool a sentry's eyes.
One fruit from that tree keeps me going a whole day. Kind folk in this village.
Red-Hooded Pilgrim Knight
I'm on pilgrimage to the old pillar ruins. An iron eye floating over the pillars — an ill omen.
I learned why the mossy altar's lanterns never go out — an iron box hovering over it pours out light.
My sword stays sheathed. The beasts of this forest are timid; they harm no one.
People from other times keep crossing over. There must be a rift torn in the sky.
Courier Dal-eum
The address just says 'forest village mailbox.' There are no street addresses out here.
I wanted to park by the delivery counter, but there are no roads, so I walk everywhere.
Did you see a covered car in the flower field? Looks like a coworker's, but nobody was around.
First village where I get stamps instead of signatures. Wait — were those paw prints…?
Photographer Chalna
There's a machine floating right in the middle of the fairy ring! That's a magazine cover.
The mist ghosts don't show up in photos. Just a blue glow smudged in the corner.
My phone battery is dying. I suppose this village has no outlets?
A forest goblin ran off with my lens cap. Think I can get it back?
Golden Exosuit Time Traveler
This exosuit is built for walking only. I can't keep up with the running beasts.
In the archives this forest is listed as 'the lost forest.' So this is what it was like alive.
The debris floating around the forest is from my time. It got swept here through the rift.
Wishes on the wish stone come true? In my era, stones like that are only in museums.
Crash-Landed Surveyor Rumi
My lander got caught in the time rift and broke apart. Its parts must be floating all over the forest.
My searchlight is hovering by the standing stone in the rocky fields. It still lights up.
The air in this era is sweet. I think I can switch off my filter and breathe.
I sent a rescue signal. Estimated arrival… three hundred years from now.

The Day We Moved In
The night you unpack, the sky cracks and Courier Dal-eum falls out with a parcel.
Your first night here is ending. Have you unpacked? Stars slip in nicely between the thatched roofs of this forest.
While unpacking I noticed a thin crack in the sky. Is it the trail of a shooting star?
A crack... this old man has never seen one. First put at least one piece of furniture in your house. Once the house stands, the heart settles.
Aaah! Where am I? I'm Courier Dal-eum! The sky split open and I fell down with this parcel!
The addressee is "the new neighbor of this village", but the sent date is far in the future. Light letters are leaking out of the box.
A parcel from the far future. Tell the counter and start with a delivery. You may see something along the way.
The Old Postbox in the Ruins
Where the light letter points - the old postbox in the tower ruins, piled with letters from many ages.
There is a place the light letter points to - the old postbox in the tower ruins. They say letters that passed here long ago are still piled up.
Past the silver-grass windfield to the ruins! They say an old public phone stands beside the ruins. Why is the postbox next to a phone?
The postbox was really there. Inside are brush-written letters, courier slips and letters stamped with glowing hologram seals, all mixed.
Letters of many ages piled in a single box. Left abandoned for so long, it must have become a postbox between ages.
Then is the crack in the sky the road this postbox called? Let's deliver these letters to the village!
The Fox Monk's Spring Market
Hoyeon slips through the crack and sells "things that lost their age". A flower-viewing festival opens the market.
Well, I've slipped through the crack. I'm Hoyeon the Fox Peddler, a peddler of things that lost their age. This light fan is from the future, and that old bell is from this land.
I heard a Samjinnal flower festival is coming. Could the market open on that day?
Gather just five flowers. I'll spread out a flower stall for the festival.
I set up the stall beside the festival signboard. A market with a loudspeaker - the sound carries far. After the festival, may I trade in this village?
New neighbors are welcome here. We'll give Hoyeon's stall a place in the village shop row.
The festival is over. One light fan is left, please take it as a gift.
I felt a resident's heart connect with mine. This village is getting better.
Filling the Archive
K-7 falls in and shows the record "The Vanished Forest". Filling the archive with fossils fades a line of it.
…Landing successful. Time traveler K-7, archivist. I carry records of the future. This forest's record column reads "The Vanished Forest".
The Vanished Forest? Does that mean this village disappears?
Forgotten places are erased from the future. I confirmed that filling the archive with fossils fades that line. Would you put in three fossils?
The record board's "Vanished Forest" has faded by one line! It means this village has begun to be remembered. But I have a request.
I want to write this village's name in the future record. Will you tell me?
Telling the village's name is entrusting its future. I will decide.
Shall we tell K-7 the village's name?
Tell
Keep it secret
Photos of the Forest
Chalna tours the forest to photograph it "before it vanishes". The last shot is the night of the firefly oak grove.
Hello! I'm photographer Chalna. In the future record this forest is called "the Vanished Forest". I want to photograph it before it vanishes.
I can't tour all eight forests, so just four - the blue pine forest, the mushroom fairy valley, the giant rock pass, and last, the night of the firefly oak grove.
I hear the standing stone on Giant Rock Pass is very old. Let's go together.
A little drone floated among the fireflies in my shot! Something from another age must be recording this forest.
Your camera and the drone were photographing the same place. Maybe it means this forest is being remembered.
I'll make four photo frames for you. Hang them on the village wall and the forest won't vanish.
Beyond the Waterfall
The explorer's riddle - behind the falls, a cave with old letters and footprints from the future.
No one knows what lies beyond the waterfall. Rumor says there's a cave behind it, old writing on its walls and footprints from the future on its floor.
I'll prepare the flashlight. Let's start beside the falls.
The cave walls were full of old writing. Beside the footprints, even a light mark. It means people of many ages passed through the same cave.
There was a bundle of letters stuck in a crack of the wall, too. It might connect to the old postbox.
Let's note "the cave behind the waterfall" in the journal. Time to go find a new riddle.
Tanabata, Wishes on the Stars
Bandi the Wisp and Dudu's gang crowd in on the Tanabata night. One guest is invited to settle in the village.
It's Tanabata, so we came to wish on the stars! I'm Bandi the Wisp. I'll guide you on the night road.
Dudu the Dokkaebi Chief here! I hung magpie-bridge lanterns and switched on a found flashlight, too. Line up, kids!
They say a wish made tonight rises through the crack. I'll wish too.
The wish slid up into the crack in the sky! Fun! Might be worth living in this village!
Dudu only causes trouble, so I worry. I'll lead him well instead. May I live in this village?
With guests to share it, the village will be brighter.
Crash Landing at the Space Base
Surveyor Rumi - her rescue signal takes 300 years to arrive. Let's "post" it through the old postbox.
I'm surveyor Rumi. I crash-landed at the space base and my rescue signal takes 300 years to arrive. My radio is of this land, so the signal only goes if it's put in an old envelope.
A signal in an envelope? You mean the old postbox is the road that posts signals to the future?
Yes! First I want to fix the transmitter with three base ores. Can you help?
The signal went into the postbox! A signal in an old envelope arrives 300 years later... Now I can wait.
I'll have the survey car's parcel brought forward. Please send news by letter.
The Firefly Garden
Dr. Nabi the Entomologist searches for why fireflies are fading - light pollution leaking through the crack.
I'm Dr. Nabi the Entomologist! I'm looking for why the fireflies decline every year. Light leaking through the crack seems to brighten the night and disturb mating.
If you lend me a net, I'll catch five insects.
Please donate them to the archive for the record. Beside the old garden wall I'll try rebuilding a firefly garden.
Thanks to the insects you donated, I confirmed the light pollution hypothesis. It was the light leaking from the crack.
We can't close the crack, but we can make less light leak out.
Harvest Moon Feast
Neighbors and guests join in: a moonlit feast after growing close to someone in the village.
At harvest we return thanks for the replies we got. Let's hold the feast after you share deep feelings with one villager.
I'll handle delivering songpyeon! I learned that songpyeon are shaped differently in each age!
I never knew the full moon was this big. The moon I saw from the mothership was small.
The moon grows depending on where you watch it. It also means you've put down roots in this village.
Shard in the Northern Cave
The keeper's request, "Treasure of the Cave" - a shard of the crack lies at the end. K-7: "The crack is the road the postbox calls."
Go to the end of the northern cave. They say there are murals, and at the very end a glowing crystal is embedded.
I hung a rope for you. Be careful going in.
This crystal is a shard of the crack. The crack was the road the postbox calls. If you touch the crystal, the crack may widen or grow quiet.
If I leave the crack wide open, guests of many ages will come more. If I ask for quiet, the nights will be calm.
What will you do with the crack?
Leave the crack wide open
Ask it to be quiet
The Winter of Piled Letters
Replies come from neighbors of the future - a thank-you letter for each resident.
Replies from the future have piled up in the old postbox. Would you deliver a thank-you letter to each resident?
Brush letters, courier boxes and light letters - three ages in one box! I'll load them for you.
The residents read the letters and laughed. I'll prepare a letter rack for you.
They were letters saying neighbors of the future remember this village.
Sharing Red Bean Porridge
Porridge for guests and residents - at least two guests must settle for the feast to be full.
It's time to cook the winter solstice porridge. When residents and guests gather at the pot, the feast fills up.
I brought a warming device too! So the porridge won't go cold!
With two guests settled, the feast is full. This village has grown so warm.
New Year Bows
Bow to every resident and settled guest.
It's New Year's Day. Go round bowing to every resident in hanbok and exchange new year greetings. I'll give you a lucky pouch.
I'll record the new year too. This village's new year greeting will go into the future record.
The Full Moon, the Star Postbox
On the night the moon house burns, the crack descends onto the postbox and it becomes the Star Postbox. "Vanished Forest" becomes "Connected Forest".
It's the full moon of the first month. They say when the moon house is lit, the crack in the sky descends over the old postbox.
I'll take the last photo! The instant the moon house firelight touches the crack!
The record board is changing... the words "Vanished Forest" are fading.
"The Connected Forest"! The record board words have changed. Because the crack stayed open, guests of every age gathered, and it became the Star Postbox hung in the sky.
Now this village will not be forgotten. Let's make the Star Postbox a village landmark. You are a neighbor of the Connected Forest.
"The Connected Forest"! The record board words have changed. The crack settled quietly, and the Star Postbox hangs in the calm night.
A calm night suits this village. The Star Postbox is a village landmark. You are a neighbor of the Connected Forest.
Neighbor of the Connected Forest
First Reply to the Star Postbox
A thawed morning - replies from three ages arrive all at once to last winter's letters.
This thawed morning the Star Postbox rattled by itself. Replies must have come to last winter's letters.
Delivery! The postmarks aren't from one place. Brush envelopes, courier receipt stamps, light seals - replies from three ages all at once!
Then I just hand these to the villagers one by one.
Thank you for delivering them. The faces of the recipients were like spring flowers. There is still one more reply inside the postbox - with a fox drawn on the outside.
A fox drawing means Hoyeon. It's polite to go and receive that reply in person.
Hoyeon's Reply
Hoyeon the Fox Peddler offers the old bell in thanks for last year's stall. The bell rings only when neighbors grow close.
It's a merchant's manners to hand over a reply face to face before putting it in a postbox. Thank you for giving up the stall last year. This year I'll treat you.
A treat? I only gathered a few flowers.
Gather five more flowers. I've picked out something among the things that lost their age that suits this village.
Lovely flowers. Hang petals on this old bell and it rings by itself in the spring breeze. When the hearts of neighbors connect this much, the bell makes its own sound.
Once your bond with a villager builds to about six hearts, the bell will find its voice.
The bell is ringing! The old land's bell and the future light fan's wind have mixed in one place. That is the reply. This village has become a crossing between ages.
May I receive a reply like this when I'm still lacking as a neighbor?
The reply is decided not by the receiver but by the sender. The sender was you.
Rebuilding the Old Postbox
The archive gains a line "Old postbox restoration unfinished". At the ruins, find traces where the old and the future built together.
The record board was updated. A new line appeared under "Connected Forest" - "Old postbox restoration unfinished".
The old postbox in the tower ruins is a pair with the Star Postbox. If only one stands, replies lose their way.
I'll go to the ruins and look at the collapsed spot.
Did you see a hard hat lying on the ruin stones? That's a modern construction site item. It means someone already started stacking.
A hologram piece of the blueprint came out too. A postbox built together by people of the future and the old - that's not in the records.
One more letter delivered and we can lay the first stone.
Spring When the Reply Came
The day the first stone is laid on the old postbox, a flower festival announces the new box. The archive line becomes "Stacking on".
The first stone is laid on the old postbox. Now we should hold a Samjinnal flower festival to announce the new postbox.
I'll hang the bell on a flower branch and go out. I'll make the flower cakes this time.
I'll hand out reply postcards one by one. They're stamped with this village's postmark!
The festival is over. The new line on the record board has changed - "unfinished restoration" became "stacking on".
This village is no longer a place that only receives letters, but one that sends replies. You are a neighbor who receives replies.
Next year, and the year after, I'll post letters from this village.
Neighbor Who Received a Reply
The Borrowed Camera
Chalna lends you a camera. Photograph the summer of two quiet forests.
I'll lend you my camera for a while. If you photograph the summer of two forests, the pine forest and the fairy valley, the reply album is complete.
It's my first time with a camera. Where should I shoot?
Not the eye-catching spots - the quietest place. In quiet places the ages seem to overlap.
The shade of the pines, the mushroom lights of the fairy valley... well shot! In that shade an old woodcutter passes, and in that light a future person's flashlight overlaps.
Hah, could even the lighthouse fire I watched from the deck in my youth remain in a photo? Take one of me next time.
Firefly Night Shoot
In a long-exposure firefly photo, reply lights from many ages line up.
The last of the summer photos is the night. The lights of the firefly oak grove only show with a long exposure. Just seat three fireflies in front.
I'll carry the tripod! The lightest parcel of all is the most reliable!
One shot took the whole night. But when I developed it, strange little lights lined up between the fireflies - they look like reply lights sent by many ages.
The fireflies and the replies were caught in one photo.
Tanabata, a Midsummer Reply
On Tanabata night villagers with lanterns pose before the Star Postbox - that photo is this summer's reply.
They say on Tanabata night the herdsman and weaver cross the crack in the sky. Let's spread the album out before the Star Postbox.
The last page of the reply album is a photo of everyone in the village standing with lanterns. Let's take it together!
Got it! Among the people holding lanterns, don't you feel an old painter and a person of the future are standing too? This photo is this summer's reply.
The record board was updated. "The Forest Kept in Photos" - a new photo line has appeared in the future record.
You are this village's photo neighbor. We'll slot the album onto the village library shelf.
Neighbor of the Midsummer Photo
Rumi's Reply
A reply box has reached the space base antenna - open it with an ore key, and deliver one letter before opening it.
The mothership link is caught again! They say the letter you posted last autumn reached the space base antenna. The key to the reply box is made from three lumps of ore.
Ore is plentiful among the mossy rubble and the caves.
I'll gather three lumps of ore.
The key fits! Out of the reply box came an old brush letter, Doha's photo letter, and a light letter - three letters. It says one must be delivered before it can be opened.
Delivery is my job! Since the addressee is this village, I'll stamp you as the village's own.
Harvest Moon Thanks
The harvest moon returns thanks for replies received - a feast after growing close to a neighbor.
The Reply Box at the Cave's End
The last reply box at the end of the northern cave - a letter from someone in the future.
The record says the last reply box lies at the end of the northern cave. Behind the place where you found the crack shard last year.
I'll go back into the cave.
The reply box is open. Inside a single letter - "I will not forget this forest. From the future." It isn't signed, but the handwriting resembles a village resident's.
Maybe it is a letter sent by our future selves. You are a neighbor who opens the reply of the future.
Neighbor Who Opens the Reply of the Future
Winter Letters in Return
This year we send letters first. Five deliveries.
Winter has come. This year let's not only receive letters but send them first. Please finish five deliveries.
Snow-road deliveries leave footprints, which I like. The footprints become a road.
All delivered! Every recipient's face was bright, so my delivery bag got lighter.
To a letter sent first, replies will come again from three ages.
Winter Solstice in Return
Share red bean porridge with neighbors who have grown close.
Let's cook solstice porridge and call the neighbors who couldn't come to last year's feast. The feast is a real feast only when a bond with a resident has deepened to eight.
I'll photograph the steam rising from the porridge. The ages seem to overlap inside the steam.
A bowl of porridge with the faint sound of the old bell - how well it goes. With this many neighbors gathered, this village could open a shop now.
For sailors, the solstice is the day to tie up the boat and share porridge. Today I'll moor my boat in this village.
New Year, New Letters
A letter in hand for every New Year bow.
New Year bows are the same as last year. But this year let's each carry a letter on the bowing round.
First delivery of the new year! I'll stamp with this village's postbox seal.
The New Year letters have gone out to many ages. Names I've never seen on the record board have begun writing replies.
They said new year letters come from the mothership too. This forest's postmark is popular!
The Second Full Moon
The night the Star Postbox and the old postbox stand side by side, the unfinished line becomes "Connected Postboxes".
The full moon has risen again. With the Star Postbox and the old postbox standing side by side, let's build moon houses in both places.
One line on the record board is left unfinished - "Old postbox restoration". Finish it tonight.
"Stacking on" became "Connected Postboxes"! There are no more lines to write on the record board - this forest is no longer a record but a story.
You lived two years with us. You are a second-year neighbor of the Connected Forest. The postbox will be open next year too.
Next year, and the year after, I'll post letters from this village.
Second-Year Neighbor of the Connected Forest
